title: Explainable Network Anomaly Detection Using Transformer-Based Multi-Model Architectures and XAI Integration
content: As cyber threats grow more sophisticated, the need for transparent and high-performance Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) becomes critical. Traditional signature-based methods often fail against zero-day attacks, while modern deep learning models are frequently limited by their "black-box" nature. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for network anomaly detection by integrating Transformer-based architectures—specifically DLinear, TabTransformer, GPT-2, and TST—with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques. The performance of these models was rigorously evaluated across three benchmark datasets: UNSW-NB15, NSL-KDD, and WSN-DS. Our experimental results demonstrate that the DLinear model exhibits superior consistency, achieving a near-perfect 99.9% accuracy and 100% recall on the UNSW-NB15 dataset. Additionally, the text-based representation approach of GPT-2 proved highly competitive on the NSL-KDD dataset. To ensure transparency, SHAP and LIME algorithms were integrated into the framework, revealing that features such as protocol types and connection intensity are vital in the decision-making process. This research bridges the gap between high-performance predictive modeling and interpretability, offering a robust, generalizable, and auditable solution for modern network security. The proposed multi-model architecture provides a significant contribution to the literature by providing a comprehensive and explainable defense mechanism.
